title: Exactly One Arrow! Functions Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Read out a roll number from the class register and you get exactly one name. Ask the blood group list who is group O and you might get two names, or none. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 2, Relations and Functions) we find out what makes a relation a function.

You will watch a live function test scan three relations element by element, see the same rule as one dot per column on a grid, and compare many arrows out of one element (not allowed) with many arrows into one element (fine). Then the notation f : A → B and f(a) = b with image and preimage, a step-by-step count of q to the power p functions (a JEE extra beyond the NCERT text) with all eight functions morphing live, a worked example, the exam trap about unused elements of B, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 One roll number, exactly one name
0:26 Definition: when is a relation a function?
0:49 Live: the function test on three relations
1:19 The grid picture: one dot per column
1:33 Arrows out vs arrows in
1:52 Pause and think: shared birth months
2:18 f : A → B, f(a) = b, image and preimage
2:34 How many functions? q to the power p
3:07 Worked example: is it a function?
3:50 Exam trap: unused elements of B
4:05 Where it is asked
4:15 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:57 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 17): Domain, Codomain and Range. Marks can be anything from 0 to 100, but the class only scored 41 to 96.

Video by Quest Academy.
